questions.q: What does `$(...)` do in a bash script, as used with `RESOURCE_GROUPS=$(az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv)`?
options: Command substitution — it runs the command and captures its output as a value to store
It comments out the command so it doesn't run
It runs the command in a new terminal window
It only works with PowerShell cmdlets, not az CLI commands
questions.explain: $(...) is command substitution: bash runs what's inside, and the output becomes the value assigned to the variable.

questions.q: In `az group list --query "[].name" -o tsv`, what does `--query "[].name"` do?
options: Applies a JMESPath filter that pulls just the name field out of each resource group
Renames every resource group to "name"
Deletes resource groups that don't have a name tag
Switches the output format to tsv
questions.explain: --query is az's JMESPath filter; [].name extracts the name field from every element of the returned array.

questions.q: Why use `-o tsv` instead of the default JSON output when the result feeds into a bash for loop?
options: tsv strips the JSON formatting down to plain lines of text, which a for loop can iterate over directly
tsv is required for az CLI to run at all
JSON output can't be stored in a bash variable
tsv makes the az command run faster
questions.explain: A for loop wants plain values one per line; -o tsv gives exactly that instead of JSON syntax a loop would mangle.

questions.q: In the tag-check script, what does `[ -z "$ENV_TAG" ]` test for?
options: Whether $ENV_TAG is an empty string, meaning the resource group has no Environment tag
Whether $ENV_TAG contains the word "production"
Whether the resource group exists at all
Whether the az CLI is logged in
questions.explain: -z is bash's empty-string test; if the tag query returned nothing, $ENV_TAG is empty and the group is flagged as missing the tag.

questions.q: What does the complete check-tags.sh script report when it finishes running?
options: A flat, scannable list of every resource group marked either OK with its tag value, or MISSING the required tag
A single number — the total count of resource groups
Nothing; it only modifies tags, it doesn't print anything
A JSON file saved to disk automatically
questions.explain: The script loops over every resource group and echoes either an OK line with the tag value or a MISSING line, one per group.
